reading.label: Vote type
reading.isBillReading: A stage in passing a law
reading.explain_preliminary: Preliminary reading — the first stage of a private bill. If it passes, the bill goes to committee to prepare it for the first reading.
reading.explain_first: First reading — the plenum approves the bill's principles and sends it to committee for detailed work.
reading.explain_second: Second reading — a vote on each clause and on reservations, after the committee has prepared the bill.
reading.explain_third: Third reading — the final vote; if it passes, the bill becomes law.
reading.explain_second_third: Second & third reading — the bill's final approval.
reading.explain_agenda: Motion for the agenda — a request to hold a plenum debate on a public issue. It is not a bill and has no readings.
reading.explain_noConfidence: A motion of no confidence in the government.
reading.explain_reservation: A vote on a reservation — an objection to a clause of a bill during the second reading.
reading.explain_secondaryLegislation: Approval of secondary legislation (regulations or orders) made by the executive.
reading.explain_continuity: Continuity — continuing the legislative process of a bill from a previous Knesset.
reading.explain_committeeReferral: Referring the bill to a committee for discussion.
reading.explain_decision: Approval of a Knesset motion, decision, or announcement.

statement.title: Accessibility Statement
statement.intro: "My Knesset" strives to provide a convenient and equal experience for all users, including people with disabilities, and works to make its content accessible in the spirit of equality and human dignity.
statement.conformance: The site is built to conform, as far as possible, to Israeli Standard IS 5568 and the WCAG 2.0 Level AA guidelines. It supports keyboard navigation, a semantic heading structure, image descriptions, and directionality (Hebrew and Arabic right-to-left).
statement.features: The site includes an accessibility menu offering: increasing and decreasing text size, a high-contrast mode, grayscale, link highlighting, a readable font, and stopping animations. Settings are saved in your browser.
statement.limitations: Some content originates from third parties (such as Knesset data, Wikipedia, and Wikimedia Commons images) and may not be fully accessible. We work to improve continuously.
statement.contact: Encountered an accessibility problem? We would be glad to hear from you and will address it promptly.

ministers.title: Government ministers
ministers.subtitle: {count} ministers and deputy ministers in the sitting government
ministers.norwegianNote: The Knesset has 120 members. However, under the "Norwegian Law" a minister or deputy minister may resign their Knesset seat to focus on government work, and the next candidate on their party list takes their place. That is why more than 120 people have served in the 25th Knesset: 120 sitting members, plus ministers who vacated their seats.
ministers.norwegianTag: Resigned their Knesset seat under the Norwegian Law and serves as a minister
ministers.note: Source: Knesset Open Data (KNS_PersonToPosition). Ministry names are shown in Hebrew as in the source.

budget.title: State Budget
budget.subtitle: Where the money goes — official, itemized budget data, with history and search.
budget.provTitle: Where do the numbers come from?
budget.provBody: All figures come from the Ministry of Finance open data on data.gov.il: the detailed approved budget (by ministry, area, program and budget line) for 2009–2018, and the Accountant-General's execution reports for recent years.
budget.provUnits: The detailed budget is shown as net expenditure; recent-year figures are the approved gross budget from the execution reports. Line names are in Hebrew as in the source.
budget.grossNote: Sum of the approved (gross) budgets of the 25th Knesset's years.
budget.timelineNote: 2009–2018 are net expenditure (detailed budget); 2019 onward are approved gross budget (execution reports), so the years are not directly comparable. 2020 is missing in the source.
budget.dataNote: Approved {year} budget from the Ministry of Finance, {count} budget lines. Amounts in NIS thousands.
budget.searchPlaceholder: Search a line, program or code…
budget.note2026: The 2026 budget and detailed budgets for 2019 onward have not been published as line-item open data; they are on the Ministry of Finance's Open Budget portal. The yearly totals for those years are shown here.
budget.sourceName: Ministry of Finance open budget data (data.gov.il)
budget.outlookNote: Editorial section — updated as a budget progresses. The detailed figures are added once published as open data.

lobbyists.title: Lobbyists
lobbyists.subtitle: Who lobbies the Knesset, for which firm, and on behalf of which clients.
lobbyists.explainer: A lobbyist is a person paid to advance the interests of clients — companies, organizations or groups — with MKs and committees. By law, lobbyists must register with the Knesset and disclose their clients. The list below is based on the Knesset's official lobbyist registry.
lobbyists.searchPlaceholder: Search a lobbyist, firm or client…
lobbyists.foreignBody: Beyond lobbying, foreign influence can also flow through money: donations from foreign political entities (foreign states or public bodies) to Israeli NGOs and organizations. The law requires organizations to report such donations — who gave, how much, and for what purpose — so the public can see who funds political or public activity.
lobbyists.foreignNote: Per-donation data is published by the Registrar of Non-Profits and on GuideStar and is not available here as structured open data.
lobbyists.whatForNote: What they were paid for and why: the registry lists each lobbyist's clients — the interest groups paying them to advance their positions in the Knesset — and the representation type (permanent or temporary). The client's identity indicates the interest being promoted; the registry does not list the specific bills or topics.
